title: At the land a maze of dark cunning nets
html_source:
Stephen trapped by Ireland’s religion and politics.

Refers to an explicit statement from Stephen in Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man ‘When the soul of a man is born in this country there are nets flung at it to hold it back from flight. You talk to me of nationality, language, religion. I shall try to fly by those nets’.

anchor.prefix: ge breath. He coasted them, walking warily. A porterbottle stood up, stogged to its waist, in the cakey sand dough. A sentinel: isle of dreadful thirst. Broken hoops on the shore;
anchor.suffix:
; farther away chalkscrawled backdoors and on the higher beach a dryingline with two crucified shirts. Ringsend: wigwams of brown steersmen and master mariners. Human shells.
